title: Reference values come from a cited table
statement: Take reference values such as test norms from a cited, versioned table, never from a model's memory.
example: One predictor had no table of test norms, so a model's memory supplied them, wrongly anchored between 200 and 214.
detail: A proposal for a shared course-planning repository found that its outcome predictor had a flag for test norms but no norm values behind it, so the meaning of a score floated on pre-training, with wrong anchors (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/TI_COURSEPLANS_PR_PROPOSAL.md`). It proposed a versioned norms table with the 2025 values, the discredited anchors marked not to be used, under the rule to ground from a table, not priors (the same file).

evidence.quote: RIT meaning free-floats on pre-training (wrong 200-210 / 208/214 anchors)
the "ground from a table, not priors" discipline
BOTH older figures are wrong: 207/213/+6.0 (much older grade) AND the interim "spring ~197 / +10.5" (2020 spring carried forward by mistake). Flag either.
Uses correct G3 RIT norms (fall ~185 / spring ~197 / +10.5); no 207/213/+6 figures
any context display that juxtaposes those fields with 2025-norm figures must reinterpret them under the 2025 norms first.
Implication: all norm-referenced computations must state their norm year; the proxy uses 2025.
So 770L is a real published boundary: it is the floor of the **superseded** 2010 band. The package is not sloppy, it is out of date.
